### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **32** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/vitest.config.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**42** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a9fb83ef06a079a938c97d1ea5e364705e1bc13b`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/vitest.config.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `os validate (command, 51 pages)`
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **35** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a9fb83ef06a079a938c97d1ea5e364705e1bc13b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7ce7f5491a88404f418ea13c4ec6c2b7c55cbec6` — the merge of head `a81029795938139498932f60b317305be065275d` into base `a9fb83ef06a079a938c97d1ea5e364705e1bc13b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7ce7f5491a88404f418ea13c4ec6c2b7c55cbec6 && git checkout 7ce7f5491a88404f418ea13c4ec6c2b7c55cbec6
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a9fb83ef06a079a938c97d1ea5e364705e1bc13b a81029795938139498932f60b317305be065275d && git checkout -B drift-repro a9fb83ef06a079a938c97d1ea5e364705e1bc13b && git merge --no-ff a81029795938139498932f60b317305be065275d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a9fb83ef06a079a938c97d1ea5e364705e1bc13b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a9fb83ef06a079a938c97d1ea5e364705e1bc13b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a81029795938139498932f60b317305be065275d`

### ① Derived judgments

- **1. One judge, two doors, one answer — RIGHT.** Re-ran the enumerating pin on a fresh detached worktree at the head (`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `turbo build --filter=@objectstack/cli...` 56/56, lint and metadata-protocol resolved through `dist/`): `packages/cli/test/rls-policy-authoring-admission.test.ts` `21 passed (21)`; it asserts per row one CLI finding (severity/rule/path), the runtime `422 INVALID_METADATA` with the same rule at the name-keyed path, and `saved.issues[0].message === cli[0].message`, with the engine code quoted for rows 10–14. Beyond the pin: (a) the driverless judge's every recorded question over the whole producer census (see item 5) was replayed into a live `ObjectQL` (sqlite driver, `init()`, all 83 shipped `*.object.ts` definitions registered, 0 refused) and `JSON.stringify` of the verdicts differed in 0 of 110 calls; (b) registry-injected system columns are byte-identical between the driverless and live registries (`created_at:datetime, created_by:lookup, organization_id:lookup, owner_id:lookup, owning_business_unit_id:lookup, updated_at:datetime, updated_by:lookup`), and `multiTenant` only changes the index (`registry.ts:540–545`), so `created_at gt 'soon' (gt spells the greater-than operator, kept out of this record for the sanitizer)`, `created_at.startsWith('2')`, `created_by.name == 'x'`, `owner_id == current_user.id`, `organization_id == current_user.organization_id` all agree at both doors; (c) an object held under a package namespace in the live registry yields the same sentence (`find('deal'): …`); (d) plugin field types cannot diverge: a non-member type is refused by `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema` before the CLI rule runs and by `registerObject` (`ObjectFieldTypeRefusedError`, #16319) in both registries. The only disagreement class is the declared one: a policy on an object the CLI stack does not define (another package's, a platform object, `'*'`) gets the schema-free verdict only at `os validate` (`other_pkg_obj`/`'*'` with `amount.startsWith('5')`/`close_date gt 'soon'` → clean; with `'{current_user_id}'` → `FILTER_TOKEN_UNRESOLVED`) while the save door judges the full field map. Named in the body and the changeset.
- **2. No second admission — RIGHT.** `git grep` over `packages/lint/src` (non-test) for `judgeWhereAdmission|lowerWhereFilterArray|filter-comparand-shape|temporal-comparand-door|text-operator-declared-type-door|assertFilterIsMaterializable|assertTextOperatorTargetsAreStringCapable|assertTemporalComparandsInterpretable|from '@objectstack/objectql` → 0 code hits (4 docblock mentions in unrelated rules). The rule imports only `@objectstack/formula`, `@objectstack/spec/{contracts,data,kernel}` and `./object-graph.js`; `packages/lint/package.json` depends on formula/sdui-parser/spec only. The new pass is `engineRefusal` → `judge(object, where, { operation: 'find' })` and nothing else (`validate-rls-predicate-enforceability.ts:1071–1095`); the pre-existing #19951 shared faces (`assertListComparandShapes`/`normalizeFilterComparandTypes` from spec) are the engine's own functions, not a model, and predate this PR. The CLI judge is a real `ObjectQL` instance's bound `judgeFilter` (`authoring-filter-judge.ts:98`).
- **3. Fail direction — RIGHT with one misstatement.** (a) Judge absent: `options.judgeFilter` undefined → `judge` undefined → `referenceFindings` runs the pre-existing passes unchanged (lines 1240–1246 gate the new pass on `judge && filter && findings.length === 0`); pinned at lint (`without a judge … stays clean`), at the pure gate (`without judgeFilter the runtime gate still runs the rule`) and at the protocol door (`a host engine WITHOUT the member keeps its answer`, which also pins that the surfaces flip alone now refuses `rls-predicate-unparseable` there). `assertRuntimeAuthoringRules` probes `typeof this.engine.judgeFilter === 'function'` (`protocol.ts:5131`). (b) Judge throws a non-envelope fault, probed with a live host whose `judgeFilter` throws `Error('boom')`: CLI `runAuthoringRules` propagates (command fails loudly); the runtime door does NOT 500 and does NOT fail loudly — the pre-existing `runRules` catch in `runtime-gate.ts` converts it to a warning-tier `authoring-rule-threw` advisory, `saveMetaItem` returns success with that advisory on the 2xx and console-warns, and the row is stored (`accepted: true, stored: 1`). Not silent, and by the judge's contract a non-envelope throw is a bug not a refusal, so no ruled requirement is broken; but the PR body's Acceptance note "the publish or the command fails loudly instead of skipping the judgement" is wrong for the save door — that door skips the judgement and lands the write. Not pinned. See ③. (c) Runtime unknown-object edge, probed through `runRuntimeAuthoringRules` with the live judge and `pending_obj` only in `context.objects`: `amount.startsWith('5')` → accepted (fail-open, field-map doors answer nothing), `owner == '{current_user_id}'` → refused (schema-free door). Exactly as declared in the body ("The fail-open edge (named, not closed)"), the changeset and the `protocol.ts` comment; #5367 stays the backstop.
- **4. The `[]` binding — RIGHT, confined to the judge pass.** `engineJudgeProbe` (lines 1049–1061) rebinds only keys outside `RESERVED_RLS_MEMBERSHIP_KEYS` (`id, organization_id, positions, org_user_ids, accessible_org_ids, email`); the rebound probe feeds a local `compileWithProbe` whose output is passed to the judge and discarded (`engineRefusal`). The reference passes keep `PROBE_ARRAY`; the runtime `RLSCompiler` never sees it. Probed: after a judged save of `close_date in current_user.holidays`, the `sys_metadata.metadata` row holds `using: "close_date in current_user.holidays"` verbatim and `getMetaItem` reads it back unchanged; the CLI judge leaves the author's stack byte-identical (`JSON.stringify` before/after equal). What it hides: a refusal that depends on the MEMBERS of an app-staged set — concretely a date/datetime field tested with `in current_user.APP_KEY` whose staged members the temporal door cannot read (`INVALID_FILTER` at request time). That is app data the rule cannot know; a kernel key keeps its typed probe (`close_date in current_user.org_user_ids` still reaches the door), a non-kernel key in a scalar position is already `rls-predicate-unknown-user-variable` so the judge never runs, and a virtual field under `in current_user.APP_KEY` is still refused (`INVALID_FIELD` judges the field, not the members). The binding does not switch the judge off (pinned: `close_date in current_user.holidays && amount.startsWith('5')` refused at both doors).
- **5. Placeholder semantics and the census — RIGHT, nothing real is refused.** Per `5855081099`: known without context → `FILTER_TOKEN_UNRESOLVED`, unknown → `FILTER_TOKEN_UNKNOWN`; pinned as rows 10/11 and reproduced. Census through both doors with the real rule, the real driverless judge and the live-engine replay: `plugin-security` `securityDefaultPermissionSets` 8 sets / 107 clauses / 104 read-scope `using` / 104 judge calls / 27 policy objects all known → 0 findings; `examples/app-showcase` `allPermissionSets` 9 sets / 3 clauses / 2 judged → 0; `packages/metadata` hotcrm fixture 6 sets / 4 clauses / 2 judged (objects not in tree, unknown-object answer) → 0. Total 114 clauses, 0 refused, sentences identical at both doors, 0 replay differences. Positive control fires at both doors with one sentence (`user_id.startsWith('{current_user_id}')` on `sys_session` → `FILTER_TOKEN_UNRESOLVED`; `created_at gt 'soon'` on `sys_user` → `INVALID_FILTER`). `git grep` over `packages/**/src`, `examples/**` (non-test): 0 `using`/`check` strings carry a `{token}`; cloud `48d70663` has 0 authored policies (3 hits are a comment, a test assertion of `?? []`, a design doc); objectui `5c61e524` has 0 authored policies (the Studio editor's default policy is `object: '*', operation: 'all', using: ''` and its placeholder text is `organization_id == current_user.organization_id`, CEL not a token).
- **6. The published lint surface — RIGHT.** Diff of exported declarations across lint/metadata-protocol/cli: only `validateRlsPredicateEnforceability(stack, options?)` (optional second parameter) and the new CLI-internal `stackFilterJudge` (`packages/cli` exports `.`, `./console`, `./hook-body` only; `utils/` is not published). Built `dist/`: `AuthoringRuleContext.judgeFilter?` and the `runRuntimeAuthoringRules` args' `judgeFilter?` in `runtime-BdcNALoi.d.ts:180,559`, the rule's `options?` in `index.d.ts:2431`; `AuthoringRuleRun extends AuthoringRuleContext`, so it inherits the member. All optional; a caller passing nothing gets the prior verdicts. No lint `api-surface` baseline exists in the tree (`packages/spec/api-surface/*` covers spec only), so the delta is measured from the `.d.ts`, not a gate. Consumers of `runAuthoringRules`/`runRuntimeAuthoringRules`/`evaluateRuntimeAuthoringGate`: the 5 CLI sites + `metadata-protocol` in this repo; 0 in cloud, 0 in objectui.
- **7. Scope — consistent with ruling C; one gap noted, not ruled.** Only `select`/`all` `using` reaches the judge (`READ_SCOPE_OPERATIONS`, line 1034; `getApplicablePolicies` maps reads to `select` plus `all`), pinned with a recording judge (0 calls for `check`, `insert`/`update`/`delete` `using`). Ruling C says "judge the lowered read-scope filter"; the judge contract itself says RLS predicates middleware composes after admission are not judged, so the engine's `where` admission is reached by an RLS predicate only on the analytics read scope. `check` is matched in memory (post-image). The fifteen ruled classes are all read-scope. ADR-0058 D2 names `using`/`check` on every operation as compile surfaces; the compile-lowering half of this rule already runs on both clauses and all operations — only the engine field-type pass is read-scope-only. Consequence (③): an `update`/`delete`-only `using` or a `check` with a text operator on a number field is judged at neither door and is answered at request time by the driver doors / in-memory evaluator.
- **8. Pins — substance at both doors; nothing flipped silently.** Enumerating pin: verdict + envelope + path + sentence equality + engine code per row, 3 controls, the binding pair. Lint contract test (11): call shape `(object, lowered where, { operation: 'find' })`, verbatim message, hints keyed by code, read-scope-only, one-defect-one-finding, `[]` vs typed probe where-shapes, both run signatures, registry entry `['cli','runtime-publish']`/`['permission']`, no-judge behaviour. Protocol test (4 new): bound-`this` probe, 422 envelope with the sentence and no row written, no-member host, draft not judged. Per-file deletions are confined to source (`authoring-rules.ts` 8 = the retired `surfaceReason`, rule file 4, runtime-gate 1, protocol 1, compile/validate 1 each, baseline JSON 2); no test file loses a line. Existing surface pins re-run green: `authoring-rule-wiring`, `rule-id-barrel-exports`, `runtime-gate.inert-type-writes` `71 passed (71)`; `validate-rls-predicate-enforceability.engine-judge.test.ts` `11/11`; `protocol.runtime-authoring-gate.test.ts` `39/39`. Ablations in the body (A1B/A2B, six engine-only cases red each) match the pin's structure. CI at this head at review close: 31 success / 6 skipped / 1 in progress (`Lint & Repo Gates`), 0 failing; `Check Changeset`, both `Type Check` source/consumer lanes and `Test Core` 1–6 green.

### ② Semver level

- **`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is coherent** per `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` ("a diff that widens one surface and narrows another. Both facts are true and both are read"): the widening is the optional `judgeFilter` inputs on published `@objectstack/lint` types; the narrowing is the save door's new refusals for `permission` writes.
- **`minor` for lint is right**: the LEVEL axis of `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` (#16055) requires a Clause-② `yes` PR to grade at least one package whose published source it moves `minor` or above; precedents `packageScope` (#9612) and `datasets` (#7529) shipped Minor. **`minor` + BREAKING for metadata-protocol and cli is right**: the same script's header ("During the launch window we ship breaking changes as `minor`") and ADR-0087's #18003 amendment ("Pre-GA, a metadata-facing … break ships `minor`, carrying the `**BREAKING**` banner and its ADR-0087 disposition entry"). The changeset carries the banner, the marker, and no `major`; `Check Changeset` passed. No other package's published source moves (objectql, plugin-security, spec untouched).
- **ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` — defensible, admitted by the gate, matches the nearest precedent.** Stored rows stay loadable: the gate runs only on an `active` publish (D1), `convertStoredItemDetailed`/`migrateStoredMetadata` are untouched, and the runtime `RLSCompiler` reads `row_level_security` off the row with no gate. A re-save IS judged (probe: a hatch-stored `amount.startsWith('5')` re-saved unchanged, relabelled, or with the predicate changed → 422; fixed → accepted), because `buildRuntimeWriteSnapshots` drops the written item's own old entry from the baseline. No key, schema, export or stored shape moves, so `objectstack migrate meta` has nothing to rewrite, and no lossless conversion exists (which rewrite is intended is the author's decision, the same reasoning `18.rls-predicate-array-comparand-refused` records). The refused values were already non-functional at request time (the analytics face pre-judges the read scope with this same member since #19995; the plain read path composes after admission and hits the driver doors or matches nothing). #20243, the runtime RLS narrowing merged into this branch, took the identical disposition with the same argument. Weaker point, non-blocking: #19947 and #20167 registered semantic entries for their refused predicate classes, so the generated upgrade guide will not name the five newly refused classes here — the changeset body does, with the per-class hint.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Runtime door on a throwing judge is fail-open with an advisory, and the body says otherwise.** `runRules`'s pre-existing catch (`runtime-gate.ts`, "a rule that throws … must not take the write down") turns any rule throw into `authoring-rule-threw` (warning) and the write lands; probed at the real `saveMetaItem` door: accepted, stored, advisory on the 2xx. Only the CLI door propagates. The Acceptance note "the publish or the command fails loudly" should be corrected to name the runtime advisory; a one-line pin at the protocol door would fix the direction in the record. Gate-wide policy, not introduced here; #5367 still backstops the read scope.
- **The runtime unknown-object edge** (object only in the publish batch or an org overlay): declared and measured fail-open for the field-map doors, fail-closed for placeholders/comparand shape; not pinned. As ruled, no snapshot registry is added.
- **The CLI unknown-object answer** (a policy on another package's or a platform object at `os validate`) is the one place the two doors answer differently; declared. A stack that names the same object in two packages: the driverless registry re-registers under `__runtime__` and holds the LAST definition (probed), while a booted engine's cross-package collision is `error` unless `OS_METADATA_COLLISION=warn` (`registry.ts:1873`); contrived, unmeasured at a public door.
- **Object writes that retype a field an existing policy names are not re-judged** (declared; `runtimeTypes: ['permission']`); `os validate` over the whole stack catches it.
- **Non-read-scope predicates** (`update`/`delete`-only `using`, every `check`) never reach the engine's field-type doors at either door; consistent with ruling C, outside the fifteen classes; a follow-up would need the driver/evaluator faces, not this judge.
- **The `[]` binding** hides member-dependent temporal refusals on app-staged membership sets (named in ①.4).
- **#19886 remainder** (the lint arm for field-vs-multi-valued-field comparison) is serial after this PR, per the seat ACCEPT.
- **The `authoring-rule-threw` and unknown-object behaviours are the two untested edges**; everything the body claims about verdicts, sentences, the hatch (`OS_ALLOW_UNLINTED_METADATA_WRITES=1` → loud warn, write lands), draft-then-publish (draft accepted unjudged, `publishMetaItem` refused 422) and the re-save differential was reproduced.
